images.caption: Entrance to the housing area known as Witch Duck Point in Virginia Beach, Virginia, USA. This is named after the place in Witch Duck Bay, located a few hundred yards to the northeast (left of photo), where Grace Sherwood, accused of witchcraft, was tried by ducking in 1706. The spelling of Witch Duck is not consistent in the region: the road is spelled Witchduck Road. There is a Sherwood Lane named after her about 150 yards to the left of the photo.
images.alt: Entrance to the housing area known as Witch Duck Point in Virginia Beach, Virginia, USA. This is named after the place in Witch Duck Bay, located a few hundred yards to the northeast (left of photo), where Grace Sherwood, accused of witchcraft, was tried by ducking in 1706. The spelling of Witch Duck is not consistent in the region: the road is spelled Witchduck Road. There is a Sherwood Lane named after her about 150 yards to the left of the photo.

images.caption: The Herb Garden at Old Donation Episcopal Church, Virginia Beach, Virginia, USA. The stone memorial on the right is to Grace Sherwood. The stone was dedicated July 10, 2014. The road behind the garden is Witchduck Road. Behind that is Sentara Independence, which is where the statue of Sherwood stands; between the road and the medical center parking lot. In the left top of the photo are some tree branches. Unseen to left of this are large bushes. Because of the trees and bushes, you can't see the statue from this exact spot. There is also some construction equipment in this photo. There is also a small statue of St. Francis of Assisi in the garden.
